User is exploring AI applications across healthcare and prefers accessible online resources, research papers, courses, podcasts, journals/conferences, and practical examples.

Main interests:
- AI-powered medical diagnosis, especially rare and undiagnosed diseases
- Machine learning/NLP using genomic data, clinical notes/EHRs, lab results, symptoms, and medical images
- Medical imaging: radiology, CT, X-ray, MRI, fundus imaging, segmentation, and detection
- Personalized/precision medicine, genomics, risk prediction, treatment optimization, clinical-trial matching, and patient stratification
- Patient engagement tools, chatbots, virtual assistants, remote monitoring, telemedicine, and health coaching
- Healthcare operations, resource allocation, scheduling, patient flow, supply chains, and administrative efficiency
- Broader challenges: data integration, validation, interpretability, ethics, regulation, bias, fairness, and clinical adoption

User is learning machine learning through a Coursera course and is interested in how ML can address rare-disease data scarcity, high-quality standardized/annotated data, transfer learning, data augmentation, and explainability. They believe AI could democratize access to specialized care through remote diagnostics, telemedicine, personalized plans, and remote monitoring, especially for rare-disease patients, while emphasizing representative datasets, algorithmic fairness, transparency, patient/clinician collaboration, and equitable deployment. They are also interested in clinical applications in cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, arrhythmias, diabetic retinopathy, and disease surveillance.

Relevant organizations/publications previously mentioned: AMA, WHO, NIBIB, RSNA, ACR, SPIE, Stanford Medicine, *Journal of Biomedical Informatics*, *Radiology: Artificial Intelligence*, *IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging*, *Healthcare Management Review*, AMIA, ACM CHIL, NIH Undiagnosed Diseases Network, Rare Genomics Institute, and Verily DeepVariant. Papers/topics previously mentioned include Rajkomar et al. (EHR diagnosis), Meystre et al. (NLP clinical decision support), Gulshan et al. (diabetic retinopathy), Rajpurkar et al.
